If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, reduce forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in the mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, increase forecasted price by 1.5–2.5% in the early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast downward by 2–3% in the late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in late horizon to capture momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in mid-horizon to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) across 7+ days, apply a 2–3% downward bias to entire forecast, especially in late horizon, to reflect sustained pessimism.
